title: Behind the Scenes: How Katie Miller's Shadow Campaign Secured the Chief of Staff Post for Stephen Miller
snippet: Following a devastating midterm election for Republicans, President Donald Trump named hardline adviser Stephen Miller as White House Chief of Staff—a move driven in part by a discreet lobbying campaign led by his wife, Katie Miller.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump’s decision to name policy architect Stephen Miller as his next White House Chief of Staff followed a focused, weeks-long lobbying campaign engineered by his wife, former administration official Katie Miller, according to multiple sources familiar with the internal dynamics.

A Quiet Campaign in the West Wing Shadow

As speculation mounted about the future of outgoing Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, Katie Miller privately urged key Trump allies to champion her husband for the top post. Sources speaking on the condition of anonymity revealed that she reached out to prominent figures—including Scott Bessent and associates close to Vice President JD Vance—asking them to encourage the president to choose Stephen Miller if a vacancy opened.

While sources emphasized that Katie Miller did not explicitly push for Wiles’ removal, her efforts escalated after Tuesday's midterm elections brought heavy losses for the GOP, prompting Trump to seek a personnel shakeup. "He started telling people he was done with Susie," said one person with direct knowledge of the conversations. "This is what happens when you get creamed."

Fallout from a Humiliating Midterm Defeat

The transition comes after weeks of rising frustration inside the White House, culminated by an unexpectedly sharp electoral defeat for Republicans. Wiles, who recently underwent chemotherapy treatment for breast cancer, had reportedly contemplated stepping down after the elections due to the grueling nature of the job.

Before settling on Miller, Trump floated a range of prospective candidates, including Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte, Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy, and New York Yankees President Randy Levine. Former Congressman Lee Zeldin and aide Sergio Gor were also briefly considered. The potential selection of Pulte, in particular, sparked concern among several West Wing advisers.

Doubling Down on the MAGA Agenda

By elevating Stephen Miller, Trump is signaling to his base that the administration intends to double down on its core platform rather than pivot to the center following the election loss.

White House spokesperson Lauren Bis defended the move, calling Miller a natural fit to lead the West Wing staff. "Stephen Miller has been a key player in delivering on President Trump’s America First agenda since day one," Bis said in a statement, highlighting his work on border security, deregulation, and crime reduction. "In his new role, he will continue to deliver historic successes for the American people."
